title: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
prompt:
You are given the `root` of a binary tree with `n` nodes, where each node has some number of coins, and the total number of coins across the whole tree is `n` (so on average every node should end up with exactly one coin). In one move, a coin can be moved from one node to a directly adjacent node (parent to child or child to parent).

Return the minimum number of moves required to make every node have exactly one coin. The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization); each value in the array is the number of coins at that node. Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to compute the minimum number of moves.

examples.explanation: The root has 2 excess coins that must each move one step to reach the two children, for a total of 2 moves.

The left child has 2 excess coins: one is needed by the root (1 move) and one must continue past the root to the right child (2 moves), plus the root itself needs 1 coin from its child (already counted) — total moves sum to 3.
A single node with exactly 1 coin already satisfies the requirement, so no moves are needed.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 100]
The sum of all Node.val equals n (the number of nodes)
hints: Think about each edge independently: some number of coins must cross it (in either direction) to balance the tree, and that number of crossings is exactly what counts toward the answer.

Do a post-order DFS where each subtree reports its 'excess' — the number of coins in that subtree minus the number of nodes in that subtree. A positive excess means coins need to flow up and out; negative means coins need to flow in from the parent.

The number of moves across the edge connecting a node to its child equals the absolute value of that child subtree's excess (since that many coins must cross that single edge, regardless of direction) — sum abs(child_excess) over every edge in the tree.

solution.approach: Do a post-order DFS where each subtree returns its 'excess' coins: (total coins in subtree) - (number of nodes in subtree). If excess is positive, that many coins must flow out of the subtree through its connecting edge to the parent; if negative, that many coins must flow in. Either way, the number of coin-moves across that single edge equals abs(excess). Sum abs(left_excess) + abs(right_excess) at every node to get the total moves, while also propagating (1 + node.val + left_excess + right_excess) upward as this subtree's own excess.
